la:noun:Tros.html:
Trōs, Trōis, m., = Τρώς,
a king of Phrygia, after whom Troy was named; he was the son of Erichthonius and grandson of Dardanus, ; ; ; .—Hence,
Trōja or Trōia, ae, f., Troy, a city of Phrygia, ; ; ; ; ; sq.—
Transf.
A place founded by Æneas in the Laurentine territory in Italy, .—
A place settled by Helenus in Epirus, ; .—
A Roman game played on horseback, a sort of sham-fight, ; ; ; ; ; cf. .—Hence,
Trōĭus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Troy, Trojan: Aeneas,; : heros,i. e. Æsacus,: sacra, (Troica, Müll.): arma,; : gaza,.—
Trōjānus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Troy, Trojan: urbs,i. e. Troy,: moenia,: regna,: opes,: bellum,; : tempora,; ; ; : judex,i. e. Paris,: ludi, i. e. the game of Troy (v. 2. c. supra), .— Prov.: equus Trojanus, for a concealed danger, a secret artifice: intus, intus inquam est equus Trojanus,. —Equus Trojanus is also the title of a tragedy of Nœvius, ; .— Subst.
Trōjāni, ōrum, m., the inhabitants of Troy, the Trojans, ; ; ; ; ; ; ; .—
Trō-jānum, i, n., a country-place in Latium, .—
Trōĭcus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Troy, Trojan: tempora,: bellum,; : Vesta,; cf. ignis,the perpetual fire which was kept in the temple of Vesta at Rome,: fata,.—
Trōs, ōis, m., a Trojan. ; ; .— Plur., ; ; ; 12, 137; Ov H. 1, 13; ; ; , 269.—
Trōăs, ădis or ădŏs, adj. f., Trojan: in agro Troade,: humus,: matres,: turba,.—More freq.,
Subst.
A Trojan woman, ; ; ; ; . —
Troas, the title of a tragedy by Q. Cicero, : Troades, the title of a tragedy by Seneca.—
The region about Troy, the Troad, ; ; ; ; . —
Trōĭădes, um, f., Trojan women, .

la:noun:tropaeum.html:
trŏpaeum or trŏphaeum, i, n., = τροπαιον.
Lit., a sign and memorial of victory, a trophy; orig. a trunk of a tree, on which were fixed the arms, shields, helmets, etc., taken from the enemy; afterwards made of stone and ornamented in the same manner,: statuere,: devictis Hispanis tropaea in jugis constituit, Dietsch: in modum tropaeorum arma imposuit,: sistere Romae tropaea de Parthis,; ; ; ; ; ; , ext. 3; 2, 2, 3.—
Transf.
A victory: nova Cantemus Augusti tropaea Caesaris,: tulit e capto nota tropaea viro,; ; : victoria, quae cum Marathonio possit compararitropaeo,; cf.: nostra sunt tropaea, nostra monimenta, nostri triumphi,; , ext. 1. —
A mark, token, sign, memorial, monument: tropaeum necessitudinis atque hospitii,: Maecenatis erunt vera tropaea fides, (4, 8), 34.

trŏpĭcus, a, um, adj., = τροπικός.
Lit., of or belonging to a turn or turning, tropical: Capricornus,i. e. where the sun turns back,; cf. id. Ecl. de Ratione Diei Anni, 2; .—
Trop. *
trŏpĭca, ōrum, n., changes, alterations: pecuniae cupiditas haec tropica instituit,.—
In the later rhet. lang., figurative, metaphorical, tropical (late Lat.): figura,: locutiones, Aug. contra Mendac. 10.—Adv.: trŏpĭcē, figuratively: loqui maluit,.
